title: What If a Unit Mix-Up Crashed a Spacecraft? NASA Lost One

scenes.text: What if a spacecraft was lost over a unit conversion? NASA lost one that way.
Mars Climate Orbiter cost 125 million dollars and launched in December 1998.
Two software components used different units. One calculated thrust in pound-seconds, the other expected newton-seconds.
The small errors piled up through almost ten months of cruising to Mars.
On September 23, 1999, the orbiter came within 57 kilometers of the surface, far lower than planned.
It broke apart in the Martian atmosphere. One metric unit, and 125 million dollars were gone.

description:
What if a unit mix-up crashed a spacecraft?
In 1999, NASA's 125 million dollar Mars Climate Orbiter was lost after two software components used pound-seconds and newton-seconds.
What should we run through next?
